heading: Thresholds
text:
Thresholds enforced by `validate_quality` live in `configs/quality_rules.yaml`, one section
per entity (`orders`, `inventory`, `customers`). Each entity defines: a business key for
duplicate detection, a timestamp column for freshness, row-count tolerance vs. the trailing
7-run median, per-column NULL rate limits, a max duplicate rate, and a `valid_values` map for
domain checks (e.g. `orders.status` must be one of PLACED/SHIPPED/DELIVERED/CANCELLED/RETURNED).

heading: Severity
text:
All checks in the current ruleset are `severity: error`, meaning any failure blocks the
`validate_quality` task and stops the DAG before `transform` runs â€” DataPilot never loads
known-bad data into `staging`/`analytics`.

heading: On-call triage order
text:
When a DataPilot pipeline fails, investigate in this order: (1) which task failed and its
exact error message (`get_task_logs`), (2) whether this is a new failure or a recurring one
(`get_recent_runs`), (3) what the data-quality checks actually measured for this batch
(`check_*` tools). Do not re-run a failed DAG until the root cause is understood â€”
`validate_schema` and `validate_quality` failures are not retryable and re-running without a
fix will fail again in the same way.

heading: Escalation
text:
Escalate to the upstream source-system owner (not the data platform team) for: schema
changes, stale/missing exports, and invalid values that look like a producer bug. Keep the
incident with the data platform team for: BigQuery quota/permission errors, Airflow
infrastructure failures, and DataPilot bugs in `sql/transform` or `sql/analytics`.

heading: Re-run policy
text:
Pipelines are idempotent per `batch_date` (`extract` deletes-then-loads the batch, `transform`
and `load_analytics` do the same). It is always safe to re-run a pipeline for a past
`batch_date` once the underlying issue is fixed.

heading: NULL spike in a required column
text:
If `check_nulls` fails, the most common cause is an upstream export that dropped a join
key (commonly `customer_id` on the orders export). Check the upstream export logs for the
same batch date before re-running. Do not backfill NULLs with a placeholder value â€” that
silently corrupts downstream joins in `analytics.orders_daily`.

heading: Duplicate spike on the business key
text:
`check_duplicates` compares row count to distinct business-key count. A sudden jump usually
means the upstream export was re-run and appended instead of overwritten, or an at-least-once
delivery retried a batch. `transform/*.sql` already de-duplicates staging with
`QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() ... = 1`, so a duplicate spike in raw is a data-freshness / upstream
signal, not a pipeline bug â€” flag it to the source-system owner rather than patching staging.

heading: Schema drift / schema_change failures
text:
`validate_schema` compares the source CSV header to `configs/pipelines.yaml -> schemas`.
A renamed or added column usually means the upstream team shipped a breaking change without
notice. `extract()` is tolerant (missing columns become NULL, extra columns are dropped), but
`validate_schema` still fails the run on purpose so a human confirms the new shape is
intentional before `configs/pipelines.yaml` is updated to match.

heading: Low volume / row-count anomaly
text:
`check_row_count` compares today's rows to the trailing median of the last 7 successful runs
(`quality.anomaly.volume_anomaly`). A drop >50% (orders) usually means the upstream source
file is partial â€” check the file's timestamp and size against a normal day before assuming
real-world demand dropped. Do not silently accept a partial file; investigate upstream first.

heading: Stale data / freshness failures
text:
`check_freshness` looks at the max timestamp in the batch. Stale data almost always means an
upstream job did not run for the batch date (a stuck cron, a paused connector) rather than a
DataPilot bug â€” check the upstream system's own run history for the same date.

heading: Invalid values (negative amounts, out-of-domain status codes)
text:
`check_invalid_values` enforces the `valid_values` rules in
`configs/quality_rules.yaml` (allowed status codes, minimum amount/stock_level). These almost
always indicate a bug in the upstream producer (e.g. a refund posted as a negative order
amount) rather than a transient blip, and should be reported to that team, not silently
filtered out downstream.

heading: Pipeline timeout during extract
text:
A `TimeoutError` in the `extract` task means the upstream export API did not respond within
the configured window. Retry once (the DAG already retries automatically); if it times out
twice in a row, the upstream export job itself is probably stuck â€” escalate rather than keep
retrying, since retries do not fix a stuck upstream job.

heading: Upstream API failure (5xx / connection errors)
text:
A `ConnectionError` in `extract` means the upstream export API returned an error (e.g. HTTP
503) after its own retries were exhausted. This is an upstream availability issue, not a data
quality issue â€” check the upstream service's status page before re-running the DAG.
